subject: general
question: On 20 January 2022, which court of India in Neil Aurelio Nunes and Ors vs. Union of India and Ors, upheld the constitutional validity of 27 per cent reservation for the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in the All India Quota (AIQ) for undergraduate and postgraduate medical and dental courses?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On 20 January 2022, the **Supreme Court** of India upheld the constitutional validity of **27 per cent reservation for the Other Backward Classes** (OBCs) in the All India Quota (AIQ) for **undergraduate and postgraduate medical and dental courses**.
 
• This decision was made in the case of **Neil Aurelio Nunes and Ors vs. Union of India and Ors**.
 
• The ruling was significant in affirming the central government's policy on reservations in educational institutions.
 
• The Supreme Court's decision ensures that OBC candidates will continue to benefit from the reservation in the AIQ seats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The All India Quota (AIQ) was introduced in 1986 under the directions of the Supreme Court to provide for domicile-free merit-based opportunities to students from any state aspiring to study in a good medical college located in another state.
 
• The AIQ consists of 15% of total available undergraduate seats and 50% of total available postgraduate seats in government medical colleges.
 
• The Supreme Court's decision supports the implementation of reservation policies aimed at promoting educational opportunities for historically disadvantaged communities.
 
• This case highlights the ongoing efforts to balance merit-based admissions with the need for social justice and inclusion in education.
